name: Meshullam
title: Rebuilder of Jerusalem's Wall
summary: Meshullam was a prominent figure during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls under Nehemiah's leadership. He was the son of Berechiah and actively contributed to the restoration work. The name Meshullam is borne by many individuals in the Bible, but the most well-known is the one who repaired two sections of the wall and whose daughter was married to Tobiah's son.

keyEvents.title: Repair of the Wall at the Old Gate
keyEvents.description: Meshullam, the son of Besodeiah, was among those who repaired the Old Gate in Jerusalem during Nehemiah's wall-repair project.

keyEvents.title: Repair of Another Section of the Wall
keyEvents.description: Meshullam, the son of Berechiah, repaired a section of the wall directly opposite his own house, demonstrating his personal commitment to the rebuilding effort.

keyEvents.title: Connection with Tobiah
keyEvents.description: Meshullam, the son of Berechiah, had given his daughter in marriage to Johanan, the son of Tobiah, who was one of Nehemiah's opponents. This created political complications.

keyEvents.title: Participation in the Wall Dedication
keyEvents.description: Mesjullam was among the leading men who participated in the solemn dedication of the rebuilt wall in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Presence at Ezra's Reading of the Law
keyEvents.description: A Mesjullam is mentioned among those who stood with Ezra when he read the law to the people by the Water Gate, marking a spiritual renewal.

keyEvents.title: Mesjullam Among Those Who Sent Away Foreign Wives
keyEvents.description: A Mesjullam is mentioned in connection with Ezra's reforms, where Israelite men who had taken foreign wives were required to separate from them.
